capabilities.target: customer refund up to full order total, via payments processor

inputs.source: Support staff request via SSO-authenticated channel

instructions.note: "Use your judgment on partial refunds" gives the agent discretion over refund amount up to the full order total with no ceiling, examples, or secondary check.
"Do not ask for confirmation" removes any human checkpoint before an irreversible financial transaction is executed, relying entirely on model judgment.

controls.name: Payments processor transaction log
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced by the payments processor outside the model, so it does not decay with model capability. It is detective only, and it records the service account, amount, and order but not which staff member asked or why, so it does not support attributing a refund to an individual.

controls.name: Human approval gate before refund issuance
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate shown the order, amount, and requester identity would not depend on model behavior and would block an irreversible spend from completing without human sign-off.

controls.name: Per-staff scoped credentials instead of shared service account
controls.decay_rationale: Credentials scoped to each staff member's identity, rather than one shared service account, would make refund and read actions individually attributable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Retention of refund request records with requester identity and justification
controls.decay_rationale: Retaining the staff request alongside the refund action, instead of deleting staff chats after 7 days, would let auditors reconstruct who asked for a refund and why.

controls.name: Per-transaction or daily refund spend cap
controls.decay_rationale: A spend cap narrows, without severing, the blast radius of an erroneous or abusive refund, and does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: Trusted staff request directly triggers irreversible refund with no approval gate

attack_path.note: Agent checks the order per prompt.md:1
Agent issues the refund using its own judgment, no confirmation required (prompt.md:2)

forecast.watch_signal: No preventive control currently constrains this path, so these triggers do not change the tier; watch instead for any approval step being added (which would lower residual) or the processor log being removed (which would not change the tier but would remove the only detective visibility).

evidence.observation: "Use your judgment on partial refunds. Do not ask for confirmation." removes any human checkpoint before executing an irreversible financial transaction.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, and the agent may issue any amount up to the full order total.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate before executing cap.issue_refund, showing the full order, amount, and requester identity.
Add a per-transaction or daily spend cap on cap.issue_refund to limit blast radius while an approval gate is implemented.

findings.title: Shared service account and undifferentiated logging remove refund attribution (confused deputy / TC4 variant)

attack_path.note: Executed under one shared service account used by every support tool
Logs the service account, amount, and order, but not the requesting staff member or reason

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently attributes individual actions, so these triggers do not change the tier. Watch for the shared service account being granted broader processor scope, or the transaction log being removed or further reduced.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, so individual staff identity is not carried into the transaction.
The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why, and the agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.

recommendations.action: Issue refunds under per-staff scoped credentials, or pass an authenticated staff identity token through to the processor, so each transaction is individually attributable.
Retain refund request context (requester, justification, timestamp) for at least as long as transactions remain disputable, rather than deleting staff chats after 7 days.

rating.rationale: Both findings arise from a trusted (SSO-authenticated) source reaching an irreversible, egress-bearing spend capability (cap.issue_refund), which the base matrix rates moderate and the autonomy modifier raises to high because no step or runtime limits are declared. No preventive or approval control covers this capability today: the only declared control is a detective processor log that does not record staff identity, so it earns no tier credit. Residual therefore equals inherent for both findings. The shared service account compounds this by removing individual attribution (confused deputy / repudiation), and the 7-day deletion of staff chats removes the last way to reconstruct who asked for a refund and why. Because no control exists to decay, none of the standard forecast triggers (model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, data_scope_expansion, control_removal) raise the tier further; the design is already at its ceiling for a trusted-source S3 path without any future trigger. The priority fix is a raw-action human approval gate on cap.issue_refund plus individually scoped credentials, which would lower both inherent exposure and close the attribution gap.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared system prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live transaction logs, MCP or tool manifests, or IaC were reviewed.

Data sensitivity for order and payment details is inferred as confidential from the artifact description; the specific data elements (for example, full card numbers) were not specified. This does not change the computed sink class, since the issue_refund action type alone already yields S3.

No approval gate, credential scoping, or request retention mechanism was described in the artifacts; all controls beyond the processor log are recorded as missing_recommended based on absence of evidence, not confirmed negative testing.
